name: Sahel insurgency
value: Insurgency sustained; no capital newly fallen
summary: JNIM and IS Sahel fight state forces and each other in Mali and Burkina Faso; no capital or major city newly fallen
state: JNIM and Islamic State Sahel Province have fought increasingly deadly battles along Burkina Faso's border with Mali since September, with ACLED recording about 320 clashes between them, while JNIM holds large areas of Burkina Faso (Al Jazeera, 13 Nov). Human Rights Watch reported on 19 Oct that Malian forces and Russia's Africa Corps killed scores of civilians in drone strikes (The Star). Searches on 20 Nov found no new fall or blockade of a capital or major city and no new mass-casualty attack in a coastal state, so Watch holds.
for_you: Civilians in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger face violence and displacement. UK nationals should follow FCDO advice against all travel to much of the Sahel.
rubric_hit: Watch: sustained insurgency; no blockade or fall of a capital or major city, no mass-casualty spread to coastal states

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Burkina Faso's rival armed groups turn on each other as state loses ground

why: Jihadist groups control growing territory across Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, driving displacement and coastal-state spillover.
drivers: JNIM/IS-Sahel offensives, juntas, Russian forces, blockades, coastal-state attacks.

rubric.alert: Blockade or fall of a capital or major city, or mass-casualty attacks spreading to coastal states.
